biography.plain_text: Andreas Liveras was a British-Cypriot entrepreneur who built his fortune in frozen cakes before founding Monaco’s Liveras Yachts. A shepherd’s son, he moved to London and rose from bakery delivery work to business ownership. He later developed Laurens Patisseries with his son. He was killed in the 2008 Mumbai attacks.

long_biography.plain_text:
At Liveras Yachts, Andreas Liveras developed a charter business for customers travelling with large parties who wanted the facilities of a luxury hotel at sea. He combined new commissions with extensive refits, adapting accommodation and services to paying guests. Before one major conversion, he put the acquired vessel into charter for several months to collect customers’ opinions, then used that experience to guide the work.

His niece, interior designer Sophia Liveras Dafnia, worked alongside her naval architect husband on the fleet. Their familiarity with returning clients shaped practical decisions: cramped cabins became larger suites, and space was devoted to treatments and relaxation.
